explanations.explanation: That's the word. The angel says those who dwell on the earth were “…intoxicated with the wine of her immorality.” (Revelation 17:2) Picture somebody who can't walk a straight line, and you've got the idea. I think it's the angel's way of showing how swept up they were.

Refreshed sounds like a nice day off with a cool breeze. That's not what the angel says. He says those who dwell on the earth were “…intoxicated with the wine of her immorality.” (Revelation 17:2) Nobody walks away from that feeling like a new person.

Nourished is what a good meal does for you. The angel picks a different word for this wine. Those who dwell on the earth were “…intoxicated with the wine of her immorality.” (Revelation 17:2) That wine isn't feeding anybody, friend.
It's the other way around, friend. John sees the beast “…covered with blasphemous names…” (Revelation 17:3) Names that honor God would be the opposite of that. So this one is false.
Right, it's false. The text says the scarlet beast was “…covered with blasphemous names…” (Revelation 17:3) That's not a name tag anybody would want. Covered, too, so there's no empty spot on it.

That's it. The woman is dressed in purple and scarlet, with gold and precious stones and pearls on top (Revelation 17:4). Scarlet is also the color of the beast she sits on (Revelation 17:3). Fancy from head to toe, and the passage keeps showing us what's under the fancy.
Blue and white is a clean, calm look, but it's not what John sees on her. The text says she was dressed in purple and scarlet (Revelation 17:4). Gold, precious stones and pearls come on top of that.

Fine white linen is a plain, simple outfit, and that's not what she's wearing. John sees her dressed in purple and scarlet (Revelation 17:4). Then come the gold, precious stones and pearls. This woman is not dressed down.

Yes. She held “…a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of her sexual immorality.” (Revelation 17:4) A golden cup sounds like something you'd want to drink from. The gold is on the outside, and what's inside is the problem.

Prayers and incense belong in a different set of golden bowls. In Revelation 5:8, golden bowls full of incense are the prayers of the saints. This cup is full of something else. The text says “…abominations and the impurities of her sexual immorality.” (Revelation 17:4)

No tears or ashes are mentioned anywhere in this cup. John sees “…a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of her sexual immorality.” (Revelation 17:4) I'd say it's a cup you hand back without a sip.

That's the city. The name on her forehead begins “BABYLON THE GREAT…” (Revelation 17:5) A name written right on the forehead, so there's no hiding it. And the text calls it a mysterious name, so we stay tuned for what the angel says about her.

Nineveh is the city Jonah was sent to preach to (Jonah 1:2). It's a real city in the Bible, but it's not the one on her forehead. The name starts with “BABYLON THE GREAT…” (Revelation 17:5) Good guess, just the wrong city.

Tyre is another city the Bible names, like when Jesus mentions Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 11:21). It's not the one John sees, though. The name on the forehead begins “BABYLON THE GREAT…” (Revelation 17:5) Different city, same Bible.

It's true. The whole name reads “…BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” (Revelation 17:5) That's a long name for a forehead. Somebody needed a big forehead.

It's actually true, friend. The name goes on past the city. It reads “…BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” (Revelation 17:5) So yes, mother of prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth is right there.

True. The angel asks, “Why are you so amazed?” and keeps going. He says, “I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and ten horns.” (Revelation 17:7) He doesn't leave John hanging.

It's true, friend. The angel notices John's amazement and asks, “Why are you so amazed?” Then he says, “I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her…” (Revelation 17:7) John gets his answers.

Destruction is the word. The beast “…is about to come up out of the Abyss and go to its destruction.” (Revelation 17:8) Coming up is not the end of the trip. It comes up, and then it goes to its destruction.

Victory is not what the angel says about the beast. He says it “…is about to come up out of the Abyss and go to its destruction.” (Revelation 17:8) The one who triumphs in this passage is the Lamb (Revelation 17:14), and we'll get there.

A throne would sound like a promotion, but that's not the angel's word here. The beast “…is about to come up out of the Abyss and go to its destruction.” (Revelation 17:8) The word is destruction, friend.

explanations.answer: those not written in the Book of Life
explanations.explanation: That's them. The angel says those who dwell on the earth “…whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world will marvel when they see the beast…” (Revelation 17:8) Those names weren't written from the foundation of the world.

That's the other group. The angel never says the ones who marvel are those with the Lamb. He says it's those “…whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world…” (Revelation 17:8) Later in the passage, the Lamb's people are called “called and chosen and faithful.” (Revelation 17:14)

The kings aren't who the angel names here. He says those who dwell on the earth “…whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world will marvel…” (Revelation 17:8) The kings show up a little later in the passage with their own part to play.
It's the opposite, friend. The angel says, “But when he does come, he must remain for only a little while.” (Revelation 17:10) So the last king doesn't get a long stay. A little while is all he gets.
That's it. Of the seven kings, the one who has not yet come “…must remain for only a little while.” (Revelation 17:10) I've seen cookies hang around longer than that.

Eight is the count. The angel says the beast “…is an eighth king, who belongs to the other seven and is going into destruction.” (Revelation 17:11) Seven kings, and the beast makes eight. His ending is the same as before: destruction.

One would make the beast the first king, but the angel counts it differently. There are seven kings already (Revelation 17:10), and the beast “…is an eighth king, who belongs to the other seven…” (Revelation 17:11) So it comes in at number eight, friend.

Ten is a different group in this passage. The ten horns are ten kings (Revelation 17:12). The beast is called “…an eighth king, who belongs to the other seven…” (Revelation 17:11) Keep the numbers straight, because this angel is counting.

One hour. The ten kings “…will receive one hour of authority as kings along with the beast.” (Revelation 17:12) That's a short shift, shorter than a lot of meetings. They haven't even received a kingdom yet, and the clock is already tiny.

Seven years would be a long run, but it's not in this verse. The angel says the ten kings “…will receive one hour of authority as kings along with the beast.” (Revelation 17:12) One hour is a lot shorter than seven years.

Forty days shows up in other places in the Bible, like when Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights (Matthew 4:2). It's not the number here. The angel says the ten kings “…will receive one hour of authority as kings along with the beast.” (Revelation 17:12) One hour, friend.
The beast it is. The angel says, “These kings have one purpose: to yield their power and authority to the beast.” (Revelation 17:13) All ten, one purpose, and the beast is where it all goes.
It's the reverse. The ten kings yield their power to the beast. They don't give it to the Lamb. The angel says they “…will make war against the Lamb…” (Revelation 17:14)

The woman isn't who gets their power. The angel says, “These kings have one purpose: to yield their power and authority to the beast.” (Revelation 17:13) And later the ten horns and the beast “…will hate the prostitute.” (Revelation 17:16)

True. The angel says the ten kings “…will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will triumph over them…” (Revelation 17:14) Ten kings, a beast, a war, and the Lamb still triumphs. That's the end of that story.
It's true, friend. The angel says they “…will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will triumph over them…” (Revelation 17:14) They go to war, but they don't win.

explanations.answer: He rules over all lords and kings
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the angel gives. The Lamb will triumph “…because He is Lord of lords and King of kings…” (Revelation 17:14) Ten kings are big, but He's the King over every king.

explanations.answer: the ten kings turn on each other
explanations.explanation: The angel doesn't say that. He says the horns and the beast hate the prostitute (Revelation 17:16), but that's not the reason for the Lamb's triumph. The reason is “…because He is Lord of lords and King of kings…” (Revelation 17:14)

explanations.answer: the angels fight the battle for Him
explanations.explanation: The angel doesn't give that reason. He says the Lamb will triumph “…because He is Lord of lords and King of kings…” (Revelation 17:14) It's about who He is. He will be accompanied by His called and chosen and faithful ones.
True. The angel says, “…He will be accompanied by His called and chosen and faithful ones.” (Revelation 17:14) Called, chosen and faithful, and they're with Him. That's a good group to be in.
It's actually true, friend. The angel says the Lamb “…will be accompanied by His called and chosen and faithful ones.” (Revelation 17:14) He's not alone on this one.

explanations.answer: peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues
explanations.explanation: That's how the angel explains it. “The waters you saw, where the prostitute was seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.” (Revelation 17:15) So no swimming gear needed. The many waters are people from everywhere.

explanations.answer: the seas and rivers of the whole earth
explanations.explanation: Seas and rivers sound reasonable, but the angel says something different. The waters “…are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.” (Revelation 17:15) They aren't actual water.

explanations.answer: the tears of the saints and witnesses
explanations.explanation: The text never says the waters are tears. The angel says they are “…peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.” (Revelation 17:15) It's a big list of people, from all over.

God. The angel says, “For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose by uniting to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.” (Revelation 17:17) The beast and the kings may look like they're running things. The angel says it's God's purpose being carried out.

The dragon is a figure from earlier in Revelation, called the ancient serpent, the devil and Satan (Revelation 12:9). But the angel names someone else here. He says, “For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose…” (Revelation 17:17)

The false prophet shows up in Revelation 16:13, but he's not who the angel names here. The angel says, “For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose by uniting to give their kingdom to the beast…” (Revelation 17:17) So it's God's purpose, friend.

explanations.answer: the great city that rules the kings of the earth
explanations.explanation: That's what the angel says. “And the woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.” (Revelation 17:18) So the woman is a city, and it rules over kings. That helps explain why her forehead carried a city's name.

explanations.answer: a queen from a land far beyond the sea
explanations.explanation: The angel never calls her a queen. He says, “And the woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.” (Revelation 17:18) A city, not a person with a crown.

explanations.answer: an idol the kings of the earth set up
explanations.explanation: No idol is mentioned in the angel's answer. He says, “And the woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.” (Revelation 17:18) And this city rules the kings. They don't rule her.
